Getting Started

# Accessing Squarespace APIs using OAuth 2.0 

Squarespace uses [OAuth 2.0](tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749) to authorize third-party applications to integrate with Squarespace and consume Squarespace APIs.

## Terms 

|**Client** |Third-party application that needs to make Squarespace API calls. |
| --- | --- |
|**User** |Squarespace customer who wants to integrate their site with a client. |
|**Confirmation page** |Page created by Squarespace for the user to authorize ( **Allow** or **Deny** ) client access to their Squarespace account. |
|**Access token** |Short-term token to make authenticated API requests. |
|**Refresh token** |Long-term token to obtain new access tokens. |

## Instructions 

### 1\. Register the client and obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials 

Before a client can make Squarespace API calls, the client must be registered with Squarespace as an OAuth client. Start the Oauth client process [here](account.squarespace.com/developer-apps) .

* Client name
* Icon image (.png or .svg format, max size 200kb, 1:1 ratio)
* Redirect URI(s) - For example, `thirdpartyapp.com/oauth/connect`
* Initiate URL\* - For example, `thirdpartyapp.com/oauth/initiate` .
* Link to Client's Terms and Conditions
* Link to Client's Privacy Policy

\*Applies only to Squarespace partner apps. These will be linked from inside Squarespace.

We will review your registration and respond with `your_client_id` and `your_client_secret` as soon as possible. These credentials are used in the subsequent steps.

### 2\. Prompt the user to authorize client access 

The `/authorize` URL prompts the user to authorize client access to their Squarespace data and serves as the confirmation page. If a user selects **Allow** , OAuth 2.0 authentication is started between the client and Squarespace APIs. Append required and any optional parameters to the `GET /authorize` endpoint; **all parameter values should be URL-encoded** .

```
Code

`GET login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/authorize`
```

  
Query parameter

Requirement

Value

`client_id`

Required

Alphanumeric value for your\_client\_id that was supplied by
Squarespace in Step 1 .

`redirect_uri`

Required

String; the full redirect URI sent to Squarespace in Step 1 .

`scope`

Required

String; comma-separated list of client permission values (see below)
for API access. The confirmation page always displays website(s) for
user selection for `scope=website.*`

...

`state`

Required

Alphanumeric random value generated by client. You'll use it in
Step 3, Implement redirect URI , to prevent CSRF attacks.

`website_id`

Conditionally Required

Alphanumeric value for a Squarespace site ID.  
When a logged-in user initiates an OAuth connection from Squarespace, this
value is appended as a query parameter on the provided initiate URL. Partners must
pass this parameter back to the `GET /authorize` endpoint.  
If an OAuth connection is initiated by a logged-out user, Squarespace will not
include a website\_id parameter on the initiate URL. Partners should not pass any `website_id` parameter back to the `GET /authorize` endpoint in these cases. Instead, the user will be prompted to select a website
on the confirmation page.

`access_type`

Optional

String; use `offline` for long-term API access. For more
information, see Token expiration and long-term access . Omit
parameter for short-term API access.

**Authorize URL example with parameters**

_Note: Parameter values are in plain text and not URL-encoded for example purposes._

```
Code

`login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/authorize?client_id=fGBjMDBaUHli&redirect_uri=http://localhost:8090/oauth/callback&scope=website.inventory,website.orders&state=2BsmGS9AAzFppUmcoIagOL…
```

...

### 4\. Request access token 

```
Code

`POST login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/tokens`
```

...

**Parameters**

|Body |Requirement |Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
|`grant_type` |Optional |String; default is `authorization_code` ; use `authorization_code` for your first request. For long-term API access , use `refresh_token` for all subsequent requests. |
|`code` |Required if `grant_type=authorization_code` |Alphanumeric value of code passed to redirect URI. |
|`redirect_uri` |Required if `grant_type=authorization_code` |String; redirect\_uri used for the `/authorize` endpoint. |
|`refresh_token` |Required if `grant_type=refresh_token` |String; use application/json or application/x-www-form-urlencoded |
|Header | | |
|`Authorization` |Required |Follow the steps below to build the header value:

...

**Example Response**

```
Code

`{   "token_type" :  "bearer" ,   "access_token" :  "T1|Rr0Wc95uu3cSeBh06yB..." ,   // expires 30 minutes after it's created ...   "access_token_expires_at" :  "1553532363.542" , }`
```

### 5\. Make API requests 

After you obtain an access token, you can make API requests.

**Endpoint:**

`api.squarespace.com/...`

**Authorization format:**

`Bearer<space><access-token-from-tokens-response>`

Using the sample response from Step 4, `Authorization` would have the value:

`Bearer T1|Rr0Wc95uu3cSeBh06yB...`

## Token expiration and long-term access 

When a response from `POST /tokens` is received, `access_token` is only valid for 30 minutes. For long-term Squarespace API access, the client has to prompt the user to reauthorize using the `GET /authorize` endpoint or use refresh tokens.

### Refresh tokens 

To get a refresh token, add `access_type=offline` as a parameter to the `GET /authorize` request. When the client makes a `POST /tokens` call, the response includes `refresh_token` . Use the refresh token to get new tokens by making another `POST /tokens` call with the parameters below. The refresh token expires after seven days.

* `grant_type=refresh_token`
* `refresh_token=<previous-refresh-token-value>`

_**Note** : Each `POST /tokens` call with a `refresh_token` parameter results in a new `refresh_token` and `access_token` . Refresh tokens are effectively one-time use—the original refresh token is invalidated as soon as the new access token is used. If long-term API access is required, the client should replace the stored refresh token with the most recent `refresh_token` . Note that obtaining new tokens doesn't revoke existing access tokens._

MCP

# Overview of the Squarespace MCP Server 

The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants to Squarespace. It's built on the [Model Context Protocol](modelcontextprotocol.io/) , an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools, so assistants like Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT can look things up and make changes on Squarespace in the middle of a conversation.

With it, someone can describe a new business and leave the chat with a domain ready to buy, or ask "which orders still need shipping?" about their own store and get a live answer.

**[Connect a Client →](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/connect-a-client)** Add Squarespace to Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP client.

_Notice: If you are a Squarespace user who is accessing the Squarespace MCP server through an AI assistant, for example to search for a domain or manage your own website, your use is governed by our [Terms of Service](squarespace.com/terms-of-service) . If you're a developer building an experience for your users and connecting your own app or agent directly to the Squarespace MCP server, for example to add domain search to your product, your use is governed by our [Developer Terms of Use](squarespace.com/developer-terms) ._

## What you can do 

The server's tools are organized into groups. Each group has its own page describing what its tools do, what to ask for, and what to watch out for.

|Group |What it's for |Sign-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
|[Domains](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/tools/domains) |Brainstorm business names, check domain availability and pricing, and get a link to buy a domain on Squarespace. |Not required |
|[Commerce](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/tools/commerce) |Find, create, and update contacts and products, and look up orders, on one of your websites. Currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. |Required |

## How it works 

The Squarespace MCP server is a remote server. There's nothing to install. Your MCP client connects directly to:

```
Code

`mcp.squarespace.com/mcp`
```

You don't call the tools yourself. You ask the assistant for something in plain language, and it decides which tools to call and in what order. The tool descriptions the assistant needs are sent by the server when it connects, so they don't need to be copied into your prompts.

### Signing in 

The Domains tools work for anyone, with no Squarespace account required.

The Commerce tools read and change a website, so they need you to sign in with your Squarespace account. They only appear in your client once you've signed in, and they act with your own permissions: an assistant can only see and change what you could see and change yourself in that website's Commerce panel. See [Connect a Client](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/connect-a-client) .

...

## Supported clients 

Squarespace is built into Gemini as a connected app, and the Domains tools also work in Claude, ChatGPT, and any client that supports remote MCP servers. The Commerce tools are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. See [Connect a Client](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/connect-a-client) for setup steps.

[Connect a Client](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/connect-a-client)

MCP

Connect a Client 

The Squarespace MCP server is a remote server: your client connects to it over HTTPS, and there's nothing to install. In Gemini, Squarespace is already built in. For Claude, ChatGPT, and other clients, you add it with the server URL.

Gemini 

Squarespace is built into Gemini as one of its connected apps , so there's no server URL to enter.
1. On gemini.google.com , open Customize in the sidebar, then Connectors .
2. Find Squarespace and click Add .
3. In a chat, type @Squarespace or just ask for a domain.
Gemini offers Squarespace to personal Google accounts in the US, in English, on the web, mobile, and Windows apps. Only the Domains tools are available in Gemini.

Server URL 

Code

`mcp.squarespace.com/mcp`
Use this URL in Claude, ChatGPT, and any other MCP client. Menu names in each client change between releases, so the steps below may not match your version exactly.

Claude 

1. Open Settings → Connectors and choose to add a custom connector.
2. Enter mcp.squarespace.com/mcp as the server URL.
3. To use the Commerce tools, connect and sign in to Squarespace when prompted.
4. Start a new chat with the connector turned on.

Claude Code 

Add the server from your terminal:
Code

`claude  mcp  add  --transport  http  squarespace  mcp.squarespace.com/mcp`
Then run /mcp in Claude Code and choose the Squarespace server to sign in.

ChatGPT 

1. Open Settings → Apps & Connectors (or Connectors , depending on your plan and version).
2. Add a custom connector with the URL mcp.squarespace.com/mcp .
3. Sign in to Squarespace when prompted if you want to use the Commerce tools.
4. Turn the connector on for a new chat.

Any other MCP client 

Configure a remote MCP server with:
* URL: mcp.squarespace.com/mcp
* Transport: Streamable HTTP
Only the Domains tools are available in other clients. The Commerce tools are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT.

Sign in to Squarespace 

The Domains tools work without an account. The Commerce tools need you to sign in with the Squarespace account you use to manage your websites, and are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT.
When your client offers to connect or sign in, you're taken to the standard Squarespace login page. After you sign in, your client receives access to the signed-in tools and they appear in its tool list. Until then, only the Domains tools are listed.
Signing in doesn't give the assistant more access than you have. Every tool acts as you, with the permissions you have on the website it's working on. To disconnect, remove or sign out of the connector in your client's settings.
For client developers: sign-in uses OAuth 2.1. The authorization server is advertised in the server's protected resource metadata at mcp.squarespace.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp .

Verify your connection 

After connecting, try:
"Is example-test-domain.com available on Squarespace?"
The assistant should check the domain and reply with availability and pricing.
If you've signed in, also try:
"Show me my five most recent orders."
The assistant should reply with orders from your store. If it says it has no Squarespace tools for this, check that you completed sign-in and that the connector is turned on for the chat.

Next steps 

See what each group of tools can do: Domains and Commerce .

### Custom applications 

With [Squarespace's Commerce Advanced](squarespace.com/pricing) plan,
you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site.

Follow the steps below to generate an API key for a custom application.

2. In the left nav, click **Settings** ; scroll down and click **Advanced** .
3. Click **Developer API Keys** .
4. Click the **GENERATE KEY** button.
5. In the dialog, add a key name under "KEY NAME",
   and select one or more Commerce APIs under "PERMISSIONS" and permission level.
6. Record the generated key in a safe and secure place.

For security reasons, this is the only time the API key is visible.
API keys will never expire as long as the merchant site remains active.

### Commercial development 

Squarespace Extensions allow customers on any plan
to optimize and expand their site in a few clicks.
If you'd like to develop a new Extension,
start the OAuth client process [here](account.squarespace.com/developer-apps) .

### API keys are now supported for the Contacts API 

#### June 17, 2026 

The Contacts API now supports authentication with an API key, in addition to OAuth. Generate a key with the **Contacts** permission (Read Only or Read and Write) to access contact records, address books, and marketing preferences without an OAuth integration. See [Authentication and permissions](developers.squarespace.com/commerce-apis/authentication-and-permissions) for details on generating an API key and its permission levels.

# Products API overview 

**Current version: v2** | **Legacy versions: v1.1, v1.0**

_For versioning details, read the [Versioning](developers.squarespace.com/commerce-apis/versioning) guide._

Use the Products API to manage product information on a Squarespace merchant site,
including variants of a product and product images.
This API allows products to be retrieved, added, deleted, or modified
with information such as a name or URL slug, a variant's color, size, or weight, or a new product image.

## API Versions 

**v2** \- The latest version of the Products API with enhanced product type support. v2 endpoints support physical, service, gift card, and download products for most operations. Note: Download products cannot be created or deleted via v2 API.

**v1.1, v1.0 (Legacy)** \- The stable versions of the Products API. v1.0 and v1.1 endpoints will continue to be supported, but we recommend using v2 for new integrations.

results.title: Squarespace API Integration: API Keys vs OAuth, Webhooks and Rate Limits
excerpts:
1. Log in to the Squarespace site (it must be on the Commerce Advanced plan).
2. Go to Settings, then Advanced, then Developer API Keys, and click Generate Key.
3. Name the key and pick the APIs and permission level it needs. Grant the minimum: a shipping sync usually needs Orders (Read and Write) and nothing else.
4. Copy the key immediately. It is displayed once.
Every request needs an Authorization: Bearer header and a User-Agent header that describes your app. Requests without a User-Agent are rejected, and default values such as curl/7.54.0 can attract stricter rate limiting, so set your own. Plain HTTP is rejected.
curl 'api.squarespace.com/1.0/commerce/orders?paymentStates=PAID,PARTIALLY_PAID' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
  -H 'User-Agent: acme-orders-sync/1.0'
Put the key in a secrets manager, not in source control. Because it never expires, a leaked key stays valid until someone deletes it in the dashboard.

# Build on Squarespace

Everything you need to build and publish external apps — reliable APIs, clear documentation, and a marketplace to reach Squarespace's global customer base.

## What can you build on Squarespace?

### Integration, customization, or extension. Our docs can get you started, and the rest is up to you.

* 01

  #### App creation

  Use our APIs to connect your business to Squarespace and reach more customers.
* 02

  #### Advanced commerce management

  Manage your storefront's orders, inventory, transactions, and more.
* 03

  #### Website & domain reselling

  Add Squarespace websites and domains to your business offering.
* 04

  #### Custom themes & code

  Inject CSS, JavaScript, and full code blocks against the 7.1 layout model.
* 05

  #### Webhooks & automation

  Subscribe to order, inventory, content, and customer events with signed delivery.
* 06

  #### AI compatibility

  Integrate our API docs directly into Claude or ChatGPT.

## What APIs and tools does the platform include?

### Get deep control with Commerce APIs, Reseller APIs, and a reliable custom code spec.

#### Commerce APIs

Read and write orders, products, inventory, and transactions. REST endpoints, webhooks for order events, and signed payloads for safe server-to-server delivery.

#### Custom Code Spec

A documented contract for injecting code into 7.1 sites — code blocks, code injection points, and the Fluid Engine layout model. No version drift.

#### Reseller APIs

Provision, configure and bill for Squarespace sites and domains on behalf of clients. Built for companies looking to integrate our products into their offering.

## Stay in the loop

### Get notified about API updates, breaking changes, and new developer tools.

Ready to build?

Get started.

# Accessing Squarespace APIs using OAuth 2.0

Squarespace uses OAuth 2.0 to authorize third-party applications to integrate with Squarespace and consume Squarespace APIs.

## Terms

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Client** | Third-party application that needs to make Squarespace API calls. |
| **User** | Squarespace customer who wants to integrate their site with a client. |
| **Confirmation page** | Page created by Squarespace for the user to authorize (**Allow** or **Deny**) client access to their Squarespace account. |
| **Access token** | Short-term token to make authenticated API requests. |
| **Refresh token** | Long-term token to obtain new access tokens. |

## Instructions

### 1. Register the client and obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials

Before a client can make Squarespace API calls, the client must be registered with Squarespace as an OAuth client. Start the Oauth client process here.

* Client name
* Icon image (.png or .svg format, max size 200kb, 1:1 ratio)
* Redirect URI(s) - For example, `https://thirdpartyapp.com/oauth/connect`
* Initiate URL\* - For example, `https://thirdpartyapp.com/oauth/initiate`.
* Link to Client's Terms and Conditions
* Link to Client's Privacy Policy

\*Applies only to Squarespace partner apps. These will be linked from inside Squarespace.

We will review your registration and respond with `your_client_id` and `your_client_secret` as soon as possible. These credentials are used in the subsequent steps.

*Note: This review only approves your client for OAuth connections with Squarespace. It doesn't add your application to Squarespace Extensions. Listing there is a separate process.*

### 2. Prompt the user to authorize client access

The `/authorize` URL prompts the user to authorize client access to their Squarespace data and serves as the confirmation page. If a user selects **Allow**, OAuth 2.0 authentication is started between the client and Squarespace APIs. Append required and any optional parameters to the `GET /authorize` endpoint; **all parameter values should be URL-encoded**.

```
Code



GET https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/authorize
```

  

| Query parameter | Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client_id` | Required | Alphanumeric value for your\_client\_id that was supplied by Squarespace in Step 1. |
| `redirect_uri` | Required | String; the full redirect URI sent to Squarespace in Step 1. |
| `scope` | Required | String; comma-separated list of client permission values (see below) for API access. The confirmation page always displays website(s) for user selec
...
 View discounts. |   **Example:**  `&scope=website.inventory,website.orders` |
| `state` | Required | Alphanumeric random value generated by client. You'll use it in Step 3, Implement redirect URI, to prevent CSRF attacks. |
| `website_id` | Conditionally Required | Alphanumeric value for a Squarespace site ID.   When a logged-in user initiates an OAuth connection from Squarespace, this value is appended as a query parameter on the provided initiate URL. Partners must pass this parameter back to the `GET /authorize` endpoint.   If an OAuth connection is initiated by a logged-out user, Squarespace will not include a website\_id parameter on the initiate URL. Partners should not pass any `website_id` parameter back to the `GET /authorize` endpoint in these cases. Instead, the user will be prompted to select a website on the confirmation page. |
| `access_type` | Optional | String; use `offline` for long-term API access. For more information, see Token expiration and long-term access. Omit parameter for short-term API access. |

**Authorize URL example with parameters**

*Note: Parameter values are in plain text and not URL-encoded for example purposes.*

```
Code



https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/authorize?client_id=fGBjMDBaUHli&redirect_uri=http://localhost:8090/oauth/callback&scope=website.inventory,website.orders&state=2BsmGS9AAzFppUmcoIagOLj4iKII
```

# Connect a Client

The Squarespace MCP server is a remote server: your client connects to it over HTTPS, and there's nothing to install. In Gemini, Squarespace is already built in. For Claude, ChatGPT, and other clients, you add it with the server URL.

## Gemini

Squarespace is built into Gemini as one of its connected apps, so there's no server URL to enter.

1. On gemini.google.com, open **Customize** in the sidebar, then **Connectors**.
2. Find **Squarespace** and click **Add**.
3. In a chat, type `@Squarespace` or just ask for a domain.

Gemini offers Squarespace to personal Google accounts in the US, in English, on the web, mobile, and Windows apps. Only the Domains tools are available in Gemini.

## Server URL

```
Code



https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp
```

Use this URL in Claude, ChatGPT, and any other MCP client. Menu names in each client change between releases, so the steps below may not match your version exactly.

## Claude

1. Open **Settings → Connectors** and choose to add a custom connector.
2. Enter `https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp` as the server URL.
3. To use the Commerce tools, connect and sign in to Squarespace when prompted.
4. Start a new chat with the connector turned on.

## Claude Code

Add the server from your terminal:

```
Code



claude mcp add --transport http squarespace https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and choose the Squarespace server to sign in.

## ChatGPT

1. Open **Settings → Apps & Connectors** (or **Connectors**, depending on your plan and version).
2. Add a custom connector with the URL `https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp`.
3. Sign in to Squarespace when prompted if you want to use the Commerce tools.
4. Turn the connector on for a new chat.

## Any other MCP client

Configure a remote MCP server with:

* **URL:** `https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp`
* **Transport:** Streamable HTTP

Only the Domains tools are available in other clients. The Commerce tools are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT.

## Sign in to Squarespace

The Domains tools work without an account. The Commerce tools need you to sign in with the Squarespace account you use to manage your websites, and are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT.

When your client offers to connect or sign in, you're taken to the standard Squarespace login page. After you sign in, your client receives access to the signed-in tools and they appear in its tool list. Until then, only the Domains tools are listed.

Signing in doesn't give the assistant more access than you have. Every tool acts as you, with the permissions you have on the website it's working on. To disconnect, remove or sign out of the connector in your client's settings.

For client developers: sign-in uses OAuth 2.1. The authorization server is advertised in the server's protected resource metadata at `https://mcp.squarespace.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.

## Verify your connection

After connecting, try:

> "Is **example-test-domain.com** available on Squarespace?"

The assistant should check the domain and reply with availability and pricing.

If you've signed in, also try:

> "Show me my five most recent orders."

The assistant should reply with orders from your store. If it says it has no Squarespace tools for this, check that you completed sign-in and that the connector is turned on for the chat.

## Next steps

See what each group of tools can do: Domains and Commerce.

# Overview of the Squarespace MCP Server 

The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants to Squarespace. It's built on the [Model Context Protocol](modelcontextprotocol.io/) , an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools, so assistants like Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT can look things up and make changes on Squarespace in the middle of a conversation.

With it, someone can describe a new business and leave the chat with a domain ready to buy, or ask "which orders still need shipping?" about their own store and get a live answer.

**[Connect a Client →](developers.squarespace.com/mcp/connect-a-client)** Add Squarespace to Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP client.
